messages.subject_clean: The MPlus error message prior to "MODEL FIT INFORMATION"
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

Just to add to this: I'm not able to pick up the below error message with readModels:

> RANDOM STARTS RESULTS RANKED FROM THE BEST TO THE WORST LOGLIKELIHOOD VALUES
>
> 1 perturbed starting value run(s) did not converge.
> Final stage loglikelihood values at local maxima, seeds, and initial stage start numbers:
>
> 4 perturbed starting value run(s) did not converge.
>
>      THE MODEL ESTIMATION DID NOT TERMINATE NORMALLY DUE TO AN INSUFFICIENT
>      NUMBER OF E STEPS.  INCREASE THE NUMBER OF MITERATIONS.  ESTIMATES
>      CANNOT BE TRUSTED.
>
> THE BEST LOGLIKELIHOOD VALUE HAS BEEN REPLICATED.  RERUN WITH AT LEAST TWICE THE
> RANDOM STARTS TO CHECK THAT THE BEST LOGLIKELIHOOD IS STILL OBTAINED AND REPLICATED.

Right after this is a gap in the output of several lines, which is where the model fit information would normally be provided.

Best,
Jon

> Hi Kate,

> This is a good idea: it would be useful to get warnings from models that terminate normally, but with potentially dubious results. I'll put this on my to do list. My experience is that they're usually just below the "terminated normally" message, so I look there.
>
> Best,
> Michael

I am getting a similar problem using Mplus Automation, both in R and RStudio. The file I'm trying to run is for a demonstration for my work group, so it's simple:

[[init]]
iterators = xvars ;
xvars = 1:3 ;
xvarnames#xvars = "x1" "x2" "x3" ;
filename = "[[demo#xvars]].inp" ;
outputDirectory="M:/mplusauto2" ;
[[init/]]
TITLE: Predict Y2 from Y1 and [[xvarnames#xvars]]
DATA: File is ex3.11.dat;
VARIABLE: NAMES ARE y1-y3 x1-x3;
Missing are all (-9999);
USEVARIABLES ARE y1 y2 [[xvarnames#xvars]];
MODEL: y2 ON y1 [[xvarnames$xvars]];

I created this .txt file in Notepad, and am running it in an R script in Rstudio.
The error message is

> createModels("template2.txt")
Error in createModels("template2.txt") :
  Unable to find init section in template file.

I looked at the source code, and used -grep- in Linux to try to find the "[[init]]" string, and it is there...grep finds it.
I also checked the rest of my code and it seems fine.

Can you help? Thanks.

Cathy

Michael

messages.subject: Killing wayward Mplus processes kills my parallel processes
messages.subject_clean: Killing wayward Mplus processes kills my parallel processes
messages.body_plain:
I'm trying to run (using plyr and doParallel) several threads to runModels -- however, when one processes finishes, it seems to kill the others leaving me with only some of my output. It would be nice to have at least the option of not autokilling all processes named 'mplus'. Or perhaps I'm doing something wrong?

Thanks!

messages.subject: Re: Killing wayward Mplus processes kills my parallel processes
messages.subject_clean: Killing wayward Mplus processes kills my parallel processes
messages.body_plain:
Hi John,

Thanks for pointing this out. Reviewing the code, I see that runModels was killing other mplus.exe processes even after a successful exit, which is problematic. I have now changed this to only kill mplus processes on failure, and to give the user the option not to do so (set killOnFail=FALSE when calling runModels). The development version of the code should fix this problem for you. Please try it and let me know if it works.

require(devtools)

install_github("MplusAutomation", "michaelhallquist")

Best,
Michael
